name: Printing an Inverted Right Triangle Star Pattern
description:
An inverted right triangle star pattern of N rows contains N-i+1 asterisks in the i-th row. Construct a program that receives the number of rows in the inverted right triangle star pattern and prints that triangle. For example, when the number of rows in the inverted right triangle star pattern is 5, the program prints the following output:
*****
****
***
**
*
code:
#Step 1: Read the number of rows in the inverted right triangle star pattern
N = int(input("Enter the number of rows in the inverted right triangle star pattern:"))
#Step 2: Print the rows in the star pattern, one by one
for i in range(1, N+1):  
    #Step 2.1: Generate the asterisks in the i-th row 
    row = ""
    for j in range(1, N-i+2):  
        row = row + "*"
    #Step 2.2: Print the asterisks in the i-th row
    print(row)

2.content: N = int(input("Enter the number of rows in the inverted right triangle star pattern:"))
commentList:
We need to read and process the number of rows that the user enters. To read the user input from command line, we use the input() function. This statement prints a text on the screen "Enter the number of rows in the inverted right triangle star pattern:", then reads the text entered by the user.

The value that will be read is a string and we need to convert it to an integer. We convert the input string to its integer representation by using the int() function.

The conversion of the value from string to int can only be done if the string actually presents an integer. Also note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned value from the input function in a variable. We could use the input function call directly as the int function parameter.

3.content: #Step 2: Print the rows in the star pattern, one by one

commentList:
The 1st row contains N-1+1 star, 2nd row contains N-2+1 stars. In general, the i-th row contains N-i+1 stars. We can print this star pattern by using two for loops. The outer for loop will print one row in every iteration whereas the inner for loop will print N-i+1 asterisks for the i-th row.

This statement is the outer for loop. We use the range function because it generates a sequence of numbers for the for loop. Here, we want the loop to iterate through 1 to N; therefore, we need a sequence that starts at 1 with every integer number up to but not including N+1. We get this sequence by calling the function range(1,N+1).
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

5.content: #Step 2.1: Generate the asterisks in the i-th row

commentList: We need variable row to create the string that represents the i-th row of the star pattern. We need to clear the content of the string before we start generating the asterisks in each row in the star pattern.

Note that this statement cannot be placed inside the inner loop because in that case in every iteration of the inner loop variable row is set to an empty string and that means that the row content for all of rows would contain one asterisk.

We cannot place this statement outside the outer loop either because in that case the asterisks would be accumulated across rows. Therefore, the only place that we could place this statement is in the outer loop body before reaching to the inner loop.

This statement is the inner for loop. Each iteration of inner loop will concatenate the string value stored in variable row with one asterisk (*). For the i-th row of the inverted right triangle star pattern, the inner loop will iterate N-i+1 times; thus, creating a row with N-i+1 asterisks.

For the inner loop, we use the range function because it generates a sequence of numbers for the for loop. Here, we want to repeat the loop N-i+1 times; therefore, we need a sequence that starts at 1 with every integer number up to but not including N-i+2. We get this sequence by calling the function range(1, N-i+2).

Note that the name that we choose for the loop variable in the inner loop should be different from the outer for loop. Here, i is the loop variable in the outer loop and j is the loop variable in the inner loop. Also, note that the inner for loop need to be indented with respect to the outer for loop.
This statement concatenates the string in variable row with an asterisk. The resulting string will be stored in variable row.
Note that we can concatenate the content of the variables that hold string values using the + operator.
